In April 2021 the High Court acquitted Jeffrey Koo Jr., former vice chair of Chinatrust Financial Holding, in the case over the 2006 sale of structured notes tied to Mega Financial Holding, after first and second rulings of nine years and of nine years and eight months; prosecutors could appeal.
In May 2025 the Taipei District Court sentenced Jeffrey Koo Jr., former vice chairman of CTBC Financial Holding, to seven years and eight months for his role in a building purchase scandal.

Prosecutors alleged that Jeffrey Koo Jr. and three former CTBC executives inflated the value of the Chengcing Lake Building by NT$100 million, causing losses to CTBC Bank; in May 2025 the court put them under daily monitoring as flight risks.
CTBC Financial Holding reported a consolidated after-tax net profit of NT$80.619 billion for 2025, a record, with earnings per share of NT$4.08.

By May 2026 the Red Fire case against Jeffrey Koo Jr., former vice chair of CTBC Financial Holding, had run for 20 years: he was acquitted at the second and at the third retrial, the Supreme Court overturned the third acquittal too, and the High Court opened a fourth retrial.
